evidence.quote: To evaluate the device performance of PCBM, PBTI2-BTI and PCNI2-BTI as ETMs, inverted PSCs were fabricated with a device architecture of indium tin oxide (ITO)/self-assembled monolayer (SAM)/perovskite (Cs0.05 FA0.9 MA0.05 PbI3 )/ETM/BCP/Ag (Fig. 5a), in which [4-(3,6-dimet hyl-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me-4PACz) was used as the SAM. The current-density-voltage ( J-V ) curves of the champion cells are illustrated in Fig. 5b, and the corresponding device performance parameters are summarized in Supplementary Table 8. The best-performing PSC based on the benchmark PCBM exhibits a PCE of 24.3% with a V OC of 1.156 V, a J SC of 25.25 mA cm -2 and an FF of 83.10%.

ITO glass substrates were washed with soapy water, acetone and isopropanol in sequence for 30 min each and then treated with UV-ozone for a time period of 45 min. Me-4PACz (0.5 mg ml -1 ) solution was spin-coated on fresh ITO at 4,000 r.p.m. (4 s acceleration) for 30 s, followed by heating on a hot plate at 100 °C for 5 min. Then Al 2 O3/isopropyl alcohol (1:150; v:v) was spin-coated on SAMs and annealed at 100 °C for 5 min.

To evaluate the device performance of PCBM, PBTI2-BTI and PCNI2-BTI as ETMs, inverted PSCs were fabricated with a device architecture of indium tin oxide (ITO)/self-assembled monolayer (SAM)/perovskite (Cs0.05 FA0.9 MA0.05 PbI3 )/ETM/BCP/Ag (Fig. 5a), in which [4-(3,6-dimet hyl-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me-4PACz) was used as the SAM. The current-density-voltage ( J-V ) curves of the champion cells are illustrated in Fig. 5b, and the corresponding device performance parameters are summarized in Supplementary Table 8. The best-performing PSC based on the benchmark PCBM exhibits a PCE of 24.3% with a V OC of 1.156 V, a J SC of 25.25 mA cm -2 and an FF of 83.10%.

Subsequently, the PCBM (20 mg ml -1 in chlorobenzene; 1,200 r.p.m. for 60 s and 6,000 r.p.m. for 10 s), PBTI2-BTI (7 mg ml -1 in chloroform:dichlorobenzene = 1:1; 1,200 r.p.m. for 60 s and 6,000 r.p.m. for 10 s) or PCNI2-BTI (7 mg ml -1 in chloroform:dichlorobenzen e = 1:1; 1,000, 1,200, 1,500 or 2,000 r.p.m. for 60 s and 6,000 r.p.m. for 10 s) solution was deposited (thickness ~35 nm) and the resulting films were annealed at 100 °C for 5 min. Finally, 7 nm BCP and 150 nm Ag were thermally evaporated on ETM to finish the device fabrication with an active area of 15 mm 2 . For the stability test, the device was encapsulated with UV glue and polyisobutylene sealant.

The Cs0.05 FA0.9 MA0.05 PbI 3 perovskite precursor was prepared by dissolving 746.8 mg PbI 2 , 238 mg FAI, 19.8 mg CsI, 11.5 mg methylammonium iodide and 12 mg methylammonium chloride in a mixed solvent of N , N -dimethylformamide and dimethylsulfoxide (5/1; v/v) and filtered with a 0.22 μm polytetrafluoroethylene filter. The perovskite precursor solution was spin-coated on the top at 100 r.p.m. for 10 s and 5,000 r.p.m. for 30 s, then treated with 150 μl ethyl acetate dropping onto the substrate over 25 s and further annealed at 60 °C for 5 min and 100 °C for 20 min.

The current-density-voltage ( J-V ) curves of the champion cells are illustrated in Fig. 5b, and the corresponding device performance parameters are summarized in Supplementary Table 8. The best-performing PSC based on the benchmark PCBM exhibits a PCE of 24.3% with a V OC of 1.156 V, a J SC of 25.25 mA cm -2 and an FF of 83.10%.

The Cs0.05 FA0.9 MA0.05 PbI 3 perovskite precursor was prepared by dissolving 746.8 mg PbI 2 , 238 mg FAI, 19.8 mg CsI, 11.5 mg methylammonium iodide and 12 mg methylammonium chloride in a mixed solvent of N , N -dimethylformamide and dimethylsulfoxide (5/1; v/v) and filtered with a 0.22 μm polytetrafluoroethylene filter. The perovskite precursor solution was spin-coated on the top at 100 r.p.m. for 10 s and 5,000 r.p.m. for 30 s, then treated with 150 μl ethyl acetate dropping onto the substrate over 25 s and further annealed at 60 °C for 5 min and 100 °C for 20 min.

evidence.quote: Inspired by the excellent performance of PCNI2-BTI as an ETM, we further synthesized three new CNI2-based n-type polymers, PCNI2-DPP, PCNI2-BFI and PCNI2-BSeI (Supplementary Fig. 54 and Supplementary Note 1). Similar to PBTI2-BTI, these polymers showed a wide range of desirable properties as ETMs (Supplementary Figs. 55-57 and Supplementary Table 12), thus achieving a champion PCE of 25.2%, 25.6% and 26.1% for the PCNI2-DPP-, PCNI2-BFI- and PCNI2-BSeI-based devices, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 58 and Supplementary Table 13), all higher than that of the PCBM-based device.

Similar to PBTI2-BTI, these polymers showed a wide range of desirable properties as ETMs (Supplementary Figs. 55-57 and Supplementary Table 12), thus achieving a champion PCE of 25.2%, 25.6% and 26.1% for the PCNI2-DPP-, PCNI2-BFI- and PCNI2-BSeI-based devices, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 58 and Supplementary Table 13), all higher than that of the PCBM-based device.

During spin-coating, chlorobenzene was quickly dispensed 5 s before the end of the spin process as an antisolvent to assist perovskite crystallization. The films were annealed on a hot plate at 100 °C for 20 min. Next, saturated piperazinium diiodide/isopropyl alcohol solution was spin-coated on the perovskite layer at 6,000 r.p.m. for 30 s, and annealed at 100 o C for 2 min. After that, PCBM (20 mg dissolved in chlorobenzene, 1,200 r.p.m. for 60 s and 6,000 r.p.m. for 10 s) or PCNI2-BTI (7 mg ml -1 in chloroform:dichlorobenzene = 1:1, 1,200 r.p.m. for 60 s and 6,000 r.p.m. for 10 s) was deposited on top of the samples and then annealed at 100 °C for 5 min.

evidence.quote: The area of tested solar cells is 0.085 cm2.

To evaluate the device performance of PCBM, PBTI2-BTI and PCNI2-BTI as ETMs, inverted PSCs were fabricated with a device architecture of indium tin oxide (ITO)/self-assembled monolayer (SAM)/perovskite (Cs0.05 FA0.9 MA0.05 PbI3 )/ETM/BCP/Ag (Fig. 5a), in which [4-(3,6-dimet hyl-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me-4PACz) was used as the SAM. The current-density-voltage ( J-V ) curves of the champion cells are illustrated in Fig. 5b, and the corresponding device performance parameters are summarized in Supplementary Table 8. The best-performing PSC based on the benchmark PCBM exhibits a PCE of 24.3% with a V OC of 1.156 V, a J SC of 25.25 mA cm -2 and an FF of 83.10%.

Notably, the use of PCNI2-BTI as the ETM with an optimized thickness of 35 nm (Fig. 5b, Supplementary Figs. 43 and 44 and Supplementary Table 9) improves the PCE to 26.0% with a higher V OC of 1.179 V and a remarkable FF of 86.44%. This PCE is one of the highest values reported for non-fullerene ETM-based PSCs (Supplementary Table 2 and Fig. 5c). However, when PCBM is replaced with PBTI2-BTI, a significantly lower PCE of 14.1% is attained, along with a decreased V OC of 0.960 V, a J SC of 24.47 mA cm -2 and an FF of 60.30%. The inferior performance of PBTI2-BTI-based devices can be attributed to the mismatched energy level and the reduced electron-transporting capability of this ETM.

However, when PCBM is replaced with PBTI2-BTI, a significantly lower PCE of 14.1% is attained, along with a decreased V OC of 0.960 V, a J SC of 24.47 mA cm -2 and an FF of 60.30%. The inferior performance of PBTI2-BTI-based devices can be attributed to the mismatched energy level and the reduced electron-transporting capability of this ETM.

unresolved_notes: The supplied evidence establishes complete PCNI2-DPP-, PCNI2-BFI- and PCNI2-BSeI-based inverted PSCs and identifies their ETMs, but it does not explicitly establish their complete ordered layer stacks or absorber compositions. Their family records therefore preserve only the supported ETM and inverted-device identity rather than inheriting the standard PCNI2-BTI stack.

The ALD-SnO x evidence establishes PCBM- and PCNI2-BTI-based photovoltaic devices in which SnO x replaces BCP, but it does not explicitly restate the remaining ordered stack or device polarity. Those families therefore retain only the supported ETM/buffer identities and are not assumed to inherit the full standard stack.

The fabrication method reports a finished-device active area of 15 mm 2 for the standard PCBM-, PBTI2-BTI- and PCNI2-BTI designs, and states that device area was calculated by multiplying the widths of the ITO and Ag electrodes. Because this is a group-level device geometry rather than a layer property and no supported individual specimen record carries it, it is preserved here rather than assigned to the Ag layer or invented individual devices. Evidence: span-dcb51e1aeae8 and span-8ab6b0025523.

Supplementary Fig. 44 reports distributions for devices made at different spin-coating speeds and gives a combined wording of '(10 deviecs)'. A combined 10-device distribution is retained, while sample sizes of the five speed-specific mean records remain null because the evidence does not allocate 10 devices separately to each speed.

Supplementary Fig. 53 reports distributions for 12 PCNI2-BTI devices from different batches. A combined 12-device distribution is retained, while batch-specific mean records have null sample sizes because the evidence does not allocate 12 devices separately to each batch.

Supplementary Fig. 58 reports PCE distributions for PCNI2-DPP-, PCNI2-BFI- and PCNI2-BSeI-based PSCs followed by '(20 devices)'. One combined 20-device distribution record is retained with no family link because the evidence does not allocate the 20 devices among the three families.

The methods list PCNI2-BTI first-spin speeds of 1,000, 1,200, 1,500 or 2,000 r.p.m., whereas Supplementary Table 9 additionally reports a 2,500-r.p.m. population. The 2,500-r.p.m. arm is retained as a population result but is not added to the family-wide method wording.

Forward and backward J-V curves are said to be available, but the supplied evidence does not provide direction-specific numerical outcomes or map the tabulated champion values to one direction. Champion J-V observations therefore use scan_direction not_reported and are not split into unsupported forward and reverse records.

The steady-state-output and ideality-factor passages identify device types but do not establish that those measurements used the same physical specimens as the champion J-V devices. Separate measured-device records are therefore retained.
The reported finished-device active area of 15 mm 2 and tested or masked area of 0.085 cm2 are distinct source quantities and were not reconciled or converted into one another.

The general statement 'No unusual hysteresis were observed.' is not mapped to a specific device or scan direction in the supplied evidence and was therefore not propagated to every individual J-V observation. The independently tested PCNI2-BTI device retains its explicitly reported 'negligible hysteresis' outcome.

Half-cells, perovskite/ETM composite films, electron-only devices, and neat ETM films were characterization specimens rather than complete photovoltaic devices and were excluded from device families, performance observations, population statistics, and stability tests.
